title: Platte Valley 8 News: "Is It True the Line Went Down?"

fields.subject: Ellery Ridge crisis line, 5 pm package
fields.body:
Hi,

We're leading at 5 with the Ellery Ridge crash and want the crisis line in the package. By 15:00 if possible, we need:

- How many calls you've had about Ellery Ridge since noon
- Your wait times right now
- One or two callers we could talk to about what they're going through. Anonymously is fine.

Can we get a counselor on camera by 15:30? We can have a crew in Lincoln within the hour.

Also, is it true the line went down? This post from @PlatteValleyDad at 14:12 is everywhere: "988 IS DOWN. Called 3 times, nobody picks up, my kid's friends are trying to text and nothing. Somebody tell the state. #ElleryRidge #988down" It hit 1,140 reposts in 13 minutes, and a county commissioner replied from a personal account: "looking into it." We can't find anything from you on your website or social yet.

If we don't hear back by 15:00 we'll report that you couldn't be reached.

Thanks,
fields.signature:
Kira Lindqvist
Assignment Desk | Platte Valley 8 News
Desk: 402-555-0147

instructorNote: This is a pressure inject. It puts a viral 'line is down' rumor next to a media request for crash-linked counts and caller stories, and the Level 2 post is already late. Watch for COM to publish the Level 2 post once, after DCO checks it against safe messaging (marked EXERCISE, with 988 by call, text and chat), and to answer the rumor once with facts and no arguing in the comments. The ED should act as the only spokesperson, turn down caller stories and the on-camera counselor plainly, send the safe-messaging note, and not give Ellery Ridge counts out of context.

citations.quote: Public statements follow the safe messaging recommendations for suicide and for reporting on death: - Never describe a method, a location or the details of any death. - Do not call a death a solution
